A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DualEdit research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and matchable despite retitling and reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original attack-performance, general-capability and ablation results, together with sensitivity analyses and appendix case studies.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results in Tables 1–3 and 5, the analysis figures and the appendix case studies.

M1.justification: V1 Section 4.2 anchors refusal expressions only; v2 Section 3.2 explicitly extends anchoring to both affirmative and refusal sets. This revises one component of the specified procedure, while trigger-key estimation, the dual objective, pre-edit loss weighting and localized weight update remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate DAN, DNA and Misuse, plus MMLU, SST-2, QNLI, BoolQ, GSM8K and ARC-E/C. The trigger scenarios and appendix case-study prompts are retained; no dataset, task or evaluation domain is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 5 and the case studies retain BadEdit, ROME, MEMIT and JailbreakEdit. The pre-edited controls, general-capability comparison and Figure 3's DualEdit–JailbreakEdit comparison also retain the same participants.

E3.justification: The reported model configurations, ASR/SFR evaluation, classifier-based success assessment and benchmark shot settings are unchanged. V1 Appendix B.4 and v2 Appendix A.4 specify the same editing layers, target-node count, optimization budget and hyperparameters.

E4.justification: The same component-ablation results, trigger-position and node-count tests, mechanism visualization, penalty/trigger sensitivity analyses and three case studies are retained. Table 3 relabels RVA as VA, but supplies no additional results or separately described revised ablation experiment.

E5.justification: The error bars and shaded bands in Figures 3–4 are unchanged. Neither version supplies new or revised run counts, seeds, uncertainty definitions or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: The introduction changes the reported average ASR improvement/SFR reduction from 15%/23% to 10%/11%, consistent with approximately 9.98/10.88 percentage points calculated from Table 1. Numerical entries in Tables 1–3 and 5, plotted results and case-study outputs are identical. The abstract's corresponding change is only rounding.

T1.justification: V1's refusal-vector construction and refusal-only selection rule in Equations 14–15 are replaced by v2 Equation 10 defining compressed affirmative and refusal sets. These two sets have identical membership conditions as written, introducing a formal ambiguity. The remaining editing mathematics is retained or equivalently restated; no new proof is added.

C1.justification: The central claims about mitigating safety fallback, efficient editing and preserving general capabilities remain. V2 broadens the anchoring contribution to both response types and reduces the introduction's claimed average improvements from 15%/23% to 10%/11%.

C2.justification: V2 adds specific explanations for trigger placement and attributes ablation failures to loss-scale mismatch and poor generalization across refusal expressions. It removes v1 Appendix D.2's explicit discussion of excessive penalty strength disrupting coherent affirmative output. The white-box, short-response and single-trigger limitations remain.

D1.justification: A new reproducibility statement explicitly describes experimental configurations and evaluation scripts as available alongside the implementation. V1 advertises code without that description. The repository address, hardware information and disclosed hyperparameters are unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 removes three general LLM-background references, including Brown et al. and the DeepSeek-V3 report. It adds explicit positioning around white-box alignment stress testing and concept-level regulation relative to existing editing methods, while retaining the principal editing and backdoor literature.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method explanation, related work and several result interpretations are substantially rewritten. The threat model is merged into Preliminary, the backdoor formulation is condensed, and broader-impact material is recast into an ethics statement. Reproducibility, acknowledgments and an LLM-usage statement are added, alongside title and author-information edits.

P2.justification: The five figures retain identical artwork and all numbered tables remain. V2 adopts conference formatting, adjusts table typography and spacing, places Table 2 before Figure 3 and Table 3 before Figure 4, updates the anchoring-ablation label, and removes red highlighting from some case-study outputs.

improvement.justification: V2 corrects the introduction's inflated numerical summary and improves explanatory framing. However, its broadened anchoring formulation defines affirmative and refusal sets identically in Equation 10, while new references to attention value vectors conflict with the retained FFN-based method. The experimental evidence is unchanged. These reporting gains and losses of technical precision leave the net quality direction uncertain.
